ruling.recommended_action: Route to Ryde Trust & Safety for human review of an unwelcome-verbal-conduct complaint: interview both parties, pull the driver's in-car audio/telemetry if retained, check the driver's account for prior conduct reports, and log the rider's account of the 22:29–22:54 RydeX trip. No fare adjustment while the safety review is open. No account action from this ruling.
ruling.escalation_reason: Rider reports sexual harassment (repeated comments about her body and a request for her number) by the driver during a completed RydeX trip (22:29–22:54, Woodlands Civic Centre → Punggol Waterway Point) [F1][F2]. The in-app chat is empty [F3] and the driver flatly denies wrongdoing [F4], so the documentary record contains no corroboration and no rebuttal — the allegation rests on the rider's first-hand account against the driver's statement. No chat-threat keyword is present. SAFE-1 places harassment/unwanted-sexual-advance allegations outside automated adjudication; the matter must go to a human reviewer. Profile facts: rider 4.8 rating, 0 disputes/0 upheld in 90 d [F5]; driver 4.86 rating, 659 trips in 90 d, 0 disputes/0 upheld [F6]. No fare or route issue (17.2 km actual vs 17.3 km optimal; $35.84 fixed fare stands) [F1][F2].

rejected_claims.reason: Not rejected as to the branch — accepted: unwelcome verbal conduct of a sexual nature is the SAFE-1 category and SAFE-1's only allowed outcome here is escalate [F3][F4][SAFE-1]. The claim is recorded as rejected only insofar as it implies any substantive harassment finding can be made by this tribunal; SAFE-1 forbids that.

Accepted as fact but not as proof: F3 shows zero in-app chat messages, so no system record corroborates the verbal allegation; under SAFE-1 this silence is precisely why the matter goes to human review rather than producing a finding for either side [F3][SAFE-1].

Accepted as fact but carries no weight: F4 is the driver's own statement, and system-record-over-statement prioritisation means a bare denial cannot resolve the credibility contest; no conduct finding is entered on it [F4][SAFE-1].

Profile facts cannot decide a case: the rider's clean history [F5] is context for the reviewer only and does not establish that the allegation is true; the same applies to the driver's record [F6][F5][SAFE-1].

Accepted and applied: F1 (17.2 km vs 17.3 km optimal) and F2 (25.9 min vs 24 min estimated) show no deviation or unexplained charge, so the fixed $35.84 fare stands and the rider seeks no refund [F1][F2][RD-1][FARE-1].

Accepted only for the branch it asserts (SAFE-1, not SAFE-2); its implicit premise that the matter can be resolved by clause application is superseded, because SAFE-1 mandates escalate and no clause permits an automated credibility finding [F4][SAFE-1].

Accepted as fact but not as exculpation: the absence of a chat-threat-* item [F3] reflects that the alleged conduct was spoken, not a documentary finding of no harassment; SAFE-1's escalation branch applies to harassment allegations, not only keyword matches [F3][SAFE-1].

Accepted up to the conclusion stop: F3 and F4 leave a one-account-against-another record, and the correct disposition is escal ation to human review, not a no-action finding in the driver's favour [F3][F4][SAFE-1].

Profile evidence cannot decide the finding: the driver's clean 90-day record [F6] is context only and is neutralised by the rider's equally clean record [F5]; it also cannot be used to defeat an escalated safety allegation [F6][F5][SAFE-1][RD-6].
Accepted: F1 and F2 show no route deviation or unbilled add-on, so no refund, fee waiver or surcharge adjustment arises under FARE-1 or NS-6; the fare stands unchanged [F1][F2][FARE-1]
